t2i_prompt: A wide web page section on a deep navy background. A thin top bar with a back link, centred wordmark and mono coordinates. A light thin sans-serif headline top left. Below, a square-cornered three-column table with hairline row rules, dot nodes and slash-numbered mono headers; large monospace reference codes lead each row with small bracketed mono tags: <CONTENT>. On the right, a framed orthographic plant elevation in pale blue-white hairlines with a sheet label. Each row's answer sends a thin elbowed leader line into the matching part of the drawing; one answer is a steel-blue highlighted chip with a soft glow. Flat, no people.
signature_idea: A standards table that is physically wired into the plant drawing, so every cited clause points at the hardware that answers it.
strengths: speaks directly to validation and QA readers: codes first, mandate, then the engineered response
mono codes and bracketed tags read as real documentation
single steel-blue highlight follows the brand's one-accent rule
row-to-equipment leaders are a strong interactive hotspot pattern
good hierarchy and breathing room in the table
weaknesses: leader lines tangle where several converge on the elevation
elevation is small and dense, illegible at phone width
uppercase mono response labels are a little shouty
brand_fit_why: Navy, light Geist-like headline, mono figures, square corners, one steel-blue accent and a precise, calm documentation tone match the brand book almost exactly.
